articles.title: NYT vs India? Kashmir Headline Sparks Global Controversy; Western Media Hypocrisy On PoK Out
articles.description: Three words in a New York Times headline have triggered an official response from India. The headline described clashes in the region as taking place in “Pakistani Kashmir”. Within hours, the Indian Embassy in Washington pushed back, calling the wording “misleading and incorrect” and saying there is no “Pakistani Kashmir”, only Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. For India, this is not simply a debate over vocabulary. It is about how language can shape perceptions of a disputed territory. New Delhi says Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India and that Pakistan is in illegal occupation of parts of the territory. India has repeatedly objected when foreign maps, headlines or diplomatic language appear to legitimise Pakistan’s control. But where does journalism end and geopolitical framing begin? Can media use neutral administrative language when sovereignty itself is contested? And can three words in a headline influence how the world sees one of the longest-running disputes in South Asia?
